title: Tasks & Delegation Contracts
objective: After this lesson you will be able to specify tasks with expected outputs and context contracts, delegate with exactly-sufficient context, and verify handoffs mechanically before downstream work begins.
why: 'Look into this ticket' delegates nothing checkable — the agent returns prose, the next stage stalls on missing fields, and the manager re-asks. Task specs with expected outputs convert delegation into APIs: typed handoffs the next agent (or test) can consume blind. Every dropped handoff in multi-agent postmortems traces to an unspecified task.

blocks.text: A **task spec** has four slots: **description** (what, concretely), **expected_output** (exact shape — the Ch.3 Prompt-101 contract), **context** (named inputs from prior tasks, nothing more), **agent** (exactly one owner). Real CrewAI mirrors this shape (`Task(description=, expected_output=, agent=)`): the framework already thinks in contracts — this lesson teaches writing them well.

blocks.caption: contextFrom names the contract: minimal, explicit, sufficient

blocks.text: Pass **what the task needs, nothing it doesn't**: facts + relevant history, never raw dumps 'just in case'. Over-context bloats cost and invites distraction (models act on incidental details); under-context forces re-fetching and guessing. The test: delete a context item — if the task still completes identically, it never belonged.

blocks.caption: Gate handoffs mechanically — missing context fails before work, not during

blocks.text: Real CrewAI shape (for your Python project)

Production CrewAI mirrors these specs directly: `Agent(role=, goal=, backstory=, tools=, verbose=)`, `Task(description=, expected_output=, agent=)`, `Crew(agents=[...], tasks=[...], process=Process.sequential)` — with `Process.hierarchical` + `manager_llm` for Ch.5's pattern. Learn contracts here in JS miniatures; the Python translation is one-to-one because the framework was designed around the same task-as-API insight.

blocks.title: Gate the handoff
blocks.note: Run it: expect missing-both, missing-confidence, then ok with the two-field input, then ok-empty. Handoffs gate mechanically — downstream starts only on complete contracts, never on hope.

items: Task specs: description + expected_output + contextFrom + exactly one owner — delegation as API
Context exactly-sufficient: delete-to-test (removable items never belonged)
Gate handoffs mechanically: missing context fails before work starts, with named gaps

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice gater on all four cases and map each. (b) Write the draftTask spec (reply ≤60 words from decision + tone rules): description, expected_output, contextFrom, agent — with exactly-sufficient context. (c) State what breaks if draftTask also receives the raw ticket, in one sentence.
hints: Mapping: missing-both / missing-confidence / ok-two-fields / ok-empty (context-free tasks exist).
draftTask: description (draft reply per decision + tone), expected_output (plain text ≤60 words + offer included), contextFrom [decideTask.approved, decideTask.reason], agent reply-drafter.
Raw ticket alongside the decision invites contradiction (draft follows ticket mood, not the decision) plus bloat — narrowed handoffs enforce the decision.
exercise.why: Exactly-sufficient context is enforced scarcity: every included field justified, every excluded field a prevented failure mode. The raw-ticket sentence states the dual-sourcing hazard that handoff discipline exists to kill.

quiz.q: 'Look into this ticket' as a task spec fails how?
options: No expected output or context contract — downstream can't consume, verify, or test the handoff
quiz.explain: Unspecified tasks produce uncheckable prose. Contracts (shape + named inputs + owner) make handoffs APIs.

quiz.q: Draft task receives both the decision AND the raw ticket. Risk?
options: Dual sourcing: draft may follow ticket mood over the decided outcome — narrowed handoffs keep decisions authoritative
quiz.explain: Redundant context isn't free: it creates competing authorities. Exactly-sufficient handoffs enforce the decision path.

quiz.q: Handoff gate reports missing-context before downstream starts. Value?
options: Fail-fast with named gaps: debugging points at the contract, not mid-run mysteries
quiz.explain: Mechanical gates convert runtime mysteries into declared shortfalls. Missing context fails at the boundary with names attached.

summary: Tasks as APIs (description + expected_output + contextFrom + owner), exactly-sufficient context (delete-to-test), mechanical handoff gates. Delegation holds by contract.
